shift_scan.note: Secondary, deliberately conservative check. One Benjamini-Hochberg family across every scope, metric and window width. Scanning every day turns one question into ~1,800 tests, and nothing survives that correction - which is reported rather than hidden. The primary detector is PELT change-point detection, which asks the segmentation question directly instead of as a multiplicity problem.

shift_method.primary: PELT change-point detection (l2 cost, BIC-scaled penalty, min segment 4 days)
shift_method.secondary: day-by-day Welch scan with pooled Benjamini-Hochberg
shift_method.welch_p_note: p-values attached to change points are uncorrected and describe the size of a break PELT located; they do not certify its discovery
